title: Register FlashGen connector in Claude account and verify end-to-end
description: Phase 6 manual step: add https://mcp.ssaito.net/mcp as a custom remote MCP connector in Claude web or Desktop under Customize > Connectors. Enable the connector in the flashgen Claude Project. Manually verify: validate_flashcard and create_flashcard appear as available tools; validate_flashcard returns a result from Claude chat; create_flashcard produces an Anki card end-to-end after explicit user confirmation; connector is usable from Claude mobile after desktop registration.

title: Add Cloudflare OAuth auth for MCP endpoint
description: Phase 5 auth: configure OAuth-compatible authentication at the Cloudflare edge so only the owner's account can call MCP tools. Unauthenticated requests must return 401. Prefer Cloudflare Access or Cloudflare MCP OAuth tooling over hand-rolling OAuth in FastAPI. The Phase 5 smoke test for 401 on unauthenticated requests must pass after this is configured.

title: Deploy FlashGen MCP at mcp.ssaito.net over public HTTPS
description: Phase 5 infrastructure: put the service behind public HTTPS at mcp.ssaito.net. Configure DNS through Cloudflare, TLS termination, and proxying so the /mcp and /health endpoints are reachable from the public Internet. This is required because Anthropic remote connectors are reached from Anthropic infrastructure, not the local device. The Phase 5 smoke tests must pass after deployment.
notes: Server is live: uvicorn running as systemd service on 127.0.0.1:8000, cloudflared installed. Blocked on DNS: ssaito.net needs to be added to Cloudflare (nameserver change at Squarespace). Once DNS is on Cloudflare, run 'cloudflared tunnel login' then create tunnel. Bearer token written to /home/ubuntu/flashgen/.env on server.

title: Add Streamable HTTP /mcp transport endpoint for Claude connectors
description: Phase 4 implementation: expose validate_flashcard and create_flashcard over Streamable HTTP at /mcp, suitable for Anthropic remote custom connectors. Use the tool definitions from the Phase 4 design step. The endpoint must pass all tests from the Phase 4 TDD step. The transport layer must not duplicate card semantics; it delegates entirely to the shared engine.

title: Define Claude-facing MCP tool names, descriptions, and write-action semantics
description: Phase 4 design step before implementation: specify the two Claude-facing tools (validate_flashcard and create_flashcard), their full JSON input/output schemas, and tool description text. The create_flashcard description must contain an explicit write-action warning so Claude calls it only after the user has inspected the JSON and asked for card creation. This spec is the direct input to both the transport implementation and the Phase 4 test suite.

title: Wire MCP /create endpoint to create_flashcard()
description: Phase 3 implementation: add POST /create to flashgen_mcp.app that validates the request using the shared schema and calls flashgen.create_flashcard(). Return the full result JSON on success. Map engine errors (AnkiConnect unavailable, missing TTS key, deck missing) to structured HTTP error responses rather than unhandled 500s. The endpoint must pass all tests from the Phase 3 TDD step.

title: Write failing tests for MCP card creation endpoint
description: TDD first step for Phase 3. Tests cover: POST /create with valid JSON calls create_flashcard and returns the full result JSON; POST /create when AnkiConnect is unreachable returns a structured error response (not a 500); POST /create with a missing TTS API key returns a structured error naming the key. These tests must be red before the endpoint is wired. Output: tests/test_mcp_create.py.

title: Write failing tests for MCP validation endpoint
description: TDD first step for the /validate endpoint (Phase 2). Tests cover: POST /validate with valid JSON returns 200 with normalized fields; POST /validate with neither japanese nor english returns 422 with a structured error body; POST /validate with tts_provider but no tts_model returns 422 naming both required fields. These tests must fail before the endpoint is implemented. Output: tests/test_mcp_validation.py.

title: Write failing tests for card request/result schema

Tests define the contract for CardRequest (at least japanese OR english required; tts_provider+tts_model must be paired together; all optional fields accepted without error) and verify CardResult contains all expected output fields. These tests must fail before the schema implementation begins and pass only when the schema is correctly implemented. Output: tests/test_card_schema.py.

title: Harden SSH: bind sshd to Tailscale only, close public port 22
description: Make the Lightsail flashgen-mcp instance reachable for SSH only over Tailscale. Steps: (1) bind sshd to Tailscale IP + loopback via /etc/ssh/sshd_config ListenAddress, disable password auth and root login, (2) reload sshd and verify with ss -ltnp, (3) confirm a fresh ssh flashgen-mcp session still works, (4) remove the public SSH (TCP 22) rule in the Lightsail IPv4/IPv6 firewall. Break-glass fallback remains the Lightsail browser-based SSH console in the AWS UI.
notes:

- Created /etc/systemd/system/ssh.socket.d/10-listen-tailscale.conf with ListenStream reset + bind to 100.84.134.120:22 (Tailscale) and 127.0.0.1:22 only
- systemd-analyze verify ssh.socket: OK
- systemctl daemon-reload + restart ssh.socket: active
- Verified ss -ltnp shows only Tailscale + loopback bindings (no 0.0.0.0:22, no [::]:22)
- Confirmed fresh SSH session works via Tailscale (ControlMaster disabled to bypass any multiplexing)
- PasswordAuthentication and KbdInteractiveAuthentication already 'no' from cloud-init defaults

REMAINING (user to do in AWS Lightsail console, NOT done yet):

- Delete SSH/TCP/22 rule in IPv6 firewall (VM has public IPv6 2600:1f14:8c4:1200:f736:ac92:2c:d6ff, so this matters)
- Verify post-close: nc -vz -w 5 <pub-ipv4> 22 should time out; nc -vz -w 5 <pub-ipv6> 22 should time out; ssh flashgen-mcp should still work

Next session: confirm firewall closed, run verification commands, then bd close flashgen-qqq.

Both CLI and MCP must return the same error shapes. All tests from the Phase 10 TDD step must pass.

Tests cover structured error responses from both CLI and MCP: AnkiConnect unavailable returns {error: anki_unavailable, message: ...}; deck missing returns {error: deck_missing, message: ...}; duplicate note returns {error: duplicate_note, message: ...}; health endpoint returns {ok: false, reason: anki_unavailable} when AnkiConnect is down. All tests must be red before hardening implementation begins. Output: tests/test_error_contract.py.

title: Verify test coverage before engine refactor

Review coverage for create_flashcard orchestration, the AnkiConnect client, TTS routing, and furigana normalization. Identify and fill any gaps that would leave the refactor undetected. The engine refactor must not break any test that passes at this checkpoint.

title: Containerize flashgen-mcp service
description: Phase 7 implementation: create the flashgen-mcp Docker container. It runs uvicorn, reads ANKI_CONNECT_URL and API keys from environment, and reaches AnkiConnect over the private Docker network. Keep it separate from anki-headless so Anki Qt/display requirements do not leak into the MCP runtime. The Anki runtime integration tests must pass after both containers are running via docker compose.

title: Build anki-headless container with persistent profile and Xvfb
description: Phase 7 implementation: create the anki-headless Docker container with Anki, AnkiConnect, Xvfb, and required Qt runtime libraries. Mount persistent Docker volumes for the Anki profile, collection, add-ons, and media so a container restart does not require re-authentication. Provide temporary private UI access via Tailscale or SSH tunnel for initial owner login, AnkiWeb sync, and deck/model setup. AnkiConnect must be reachable on port 8765 within the private Docker network only.

title: Write integration tests for Anki runtime
description: TDD first step for Phase 7. Integration tests are skipped unless ANKI_CONNECT_URL is set. Tests cover: AnkiConnect ping returns the expected JSON shape; deck list includes the configured deck name; card count in the target deck is stable across docker compose restart (verifying profile persistence); flashgen-mcp container can reach AnkiConnect over the private network; health endpoint returns ok=false when AnkiConnect is unreachable. These tests must fail before container work begins. Output: tests/test_anki_runtime.py.

title: Write integration smoke tests for public HTTPS endpoint

Tests cover: GET https://mcp.ssaito.net/health returns 200 with ok=true; POST /mcp without an auth token returns 401; POST /mcp with a valid token returns 200. These tests define the deployment and auth acceptance criteria before any infrastructure work begins. Output: tests/test_smoke_https.py.
